summary: Summation No. 19 covers April 1947 (with economic statistics mostly for March and February) in four parts: General digest, Political, Economic and Social. April was dominated by Japan's first postwar full cycle of elections under the new Constitution: governors and mayors on 5 April, the House of Councillors on 20 April, the House of Representatives on 25 April and prefectural assemblies on 30 April, with MacArthur praising the result on 27 April. The Social Democrats became the largest lower-house party, independents dominated executive posts, and the purge screened 190,685 persons. The economic chapters show recovery driven by better coal deliveries (March coal 2,256,600 tons), postwar-peak pig iron, steel, pulp, paper and raw silk, with tightening food collection, black-market crackdowns, price rises, a new antitrust act, zaibatsu liquidation and trade-union consolidation. Social chapters give nutrition and disease data, repatriation totals, and education, religion and press developments. A historian will find detailed election returns, Diet statistics, war-crimes trial tables and sector statistics.
highlights: Japan voted four times in April 1947: 5 April for governors and mayors, 20 April for the House of Councillors, 25 April for the House of Representatives and 30 April for prefectural assemblies; MacArthur's 27 April message praised the result.

In the House of Representatives the Social Democrats won 143 of 466 seats, ahead of Liberals 132, Democrats 126, People's Cooperatives 31 and Communists 4; independents took 110 of 250 Councillor seats, Social Democrats leading the parties with 47.

Independents won 29 governorships and 3,716 village headships on 5 April; Seiichiro Yasui beat Social Democrat Daikichiro Tagawa 705,040 to 615,622 in Tokyo, and Toshibuni Tanaka became Socialist governor of Hokkaido after a run-off.

The purge screened 5,327 election candidates (190 barred) and 190,685 persons from 29 March to 26 April; Welfare Minister Yoshinari Kawai and several Democratic Party leaders were purged and an appeals board began work.

The Diet passed the antitrust Act Relating to Prohibition of Private Monopoly on 31 March, creating a seven-member Fair Trade Commission; the Holding Company Liquidation Commission took title to shares of 65 holding companies worth 5,154,152,000 yen.

March coal output was 2,256,600 metric tons, 230,500 under quota; better deliveries lifted pig iron and steel to a postwar peak, paper to 34,168 short tons and electric power to 2,432,541,000 kWh, up 21 percent.
Bank of Japan notes reached 122,400,000,000 yen on 30 April, the income-tax yield estimate rose from 4.5 to 16 billion yen, and electric power rates rose 300 percent on 1 April.

The coal miners' industry-wide contract of 12 April covered 203,316 underground workers; union membership stood at 5,326,969 in 19,983 unions on 31 March, over half of organized labor under recent agreements.

sections.title: Front matter
sections.summary: Cover for Summation No. 19 (April 1947), four-part contents and a list of 108 charts, maps and graphs.

sections.title: Part I: General
sections.summary: Digest of April 1947: no SCAP reorganization, four elections, purge and war-crimes figures, gains in coal, steel and textiles, plus health, education and press items.

sections.title: Section 1. Organization Under SCAP
sections.summary: Reports no change in the non-military organization of General Headquarters, SCAP, during April 1947.

sections.title: Section 2. Political Activities
sections.summary: Summarizes four elections choosing 232,863 officials: Social Democrats won 143 lower-house seats, 190 candidates were purged, and 46 war-crimes arrest orders were issued.

sections.title: Section 3. Economic Activities
sections.summary: Digest of land purchases of 151,566 cho, record pig iron and steel output, textile gains, Bank of Japan notes at 122.4 billion yen and 4,153,369 tons of rice collected.

sections.title: Section 4. Social Activities
sections.summary: Digest of the February nutrition survey, 62,327 repatriates, teacher conferences, shrine land notification, 18,000,000 Constitution pamphlets and press comment.

sections.title: Part II: Political
sections.summary: Covers the April elections, the 92nd Diet, the purge (190,685 screened), public safety and crime statistics, and war-crimes trials including the Tokyo Tribunal defense case.

sections.title: Section 1. Government and Politics
sections.summary: Election results for governors, Councillors, Representatives and assemblies, the 92nd Diet record, the purge of 190,685 persons screened, and labor-union endorsements.

sections.title: The General Elections
sections.summary: MacArthur's 27 April statement and tallies for the executive, Councillors, Representatives and prefectural-assembly elections, with fraud cases and run-offs in eight prefectures.

sections.title: Executive Elections (5 April)
sections.summary: 46 governors and 309 mayors and village heads elected; independents won 29 governorships, turnout 70.8 percent, Yasui beat Tagawa 705,040 to 615,622 in Tokyo, with run-offs.

sections.title: House of Councillors Election (20 April)
sections.summary: About 32,000,000 voters chose 250 Councillors; 110 independents and 47 Social Democrats won, with occupational analysis, press comment and the list of those elected.

sections.title: House of Representatives Election (25 April)
sections.summary: 1,573 candidates contested 466 seats; Social Democrats won 143, Liberals 132 and Democrats 126, with party predictions and press reaction.

sections.title: Prefectural and Local Assembly Elections (30 April)
sections.summary: 7,130 candidates ran for 2,502 prefectural seats; independents won 771 and controlled 13 assemblies, Democrats 517, Liberals 468, Social Democrats 414.

sections.title: The Diet
sections.summary: Statistics for the 95-day 92nd Diet: 173 measures submitted, 18,743 visitors, 315 petitions, eight demonstrations, and shifting party strength as the Democratic Party formed.

sections.title: The Purge
sections.summary: 190,685 persons screened 29 March-26 April; 5,327 candidates examined, 190 barred; prominent Democrats purged, about 1,160 local executives barred, and an appeals board begun.

sections.title: Labor and Politics
sections.summary: NCIU (1,643,599 members) and the General Federation endorsed candidates; labor leaders won 32 of 350 Councillor seats and 16 Representatives seats.

sections.title: Section 2. Public Safety
sections.summary: Elections passed without serious incident but produced 490 election-law cases; black-market penalties rose to 100,000 yen, 634 rail deaths in the first quarter, 129,440 February offenses.

sections.title: Section 3. Legal and War Crimes
sections.summary: War-crimes investigations (1,749 cases on hand), 46 persons ordered apprehended, trial results in Japan and the Philippines, and the Tokyo Tribunal defense case.

sections.title: Legal Affairs, Investigation, Apprehension and Prosecution of War Criminals
sections.summary: Cases rose from 1,558 to 1,749; 80 persons delivered to Sugamo; eleven Japan trials with 23 defendants; Philippine trials produced five death sentences.

sections.title: International Prosecution of War Criminals (Tokyo Tribunal)
sections.summary: Proceedings against Okawa discontinued 9 April; the Manchurian phase of the defense ended 21 April and the China phase began 22 April, with witness testimony summaries.

sections.title: Part III: Economic
sections.summary: Mostly March 1947 statistics: coal-led recovery (2,256,600 tons), tight food supply, price increases, and deconcentration through the antitrust act and holding-company liquidation, across twelve sections.

sections.title: Section 1. Agriculture and Fisheries
sections.summary: Local Land Commissions bought 151,566 cho in March, prefectural retention rates were set, March fish landings totaled 101,815 tons, and the kiji was named national bird.

sections.title: Section 2. Forestry and Mining
sections.summary: March log output 734,928,000 board feet; coal 2,256,600 tons with a 27,000,000-ton 1947-48 goal; lignite 231,197 tons; the 12 April miners' contract; oil drilling results.

sections.title: Section 3. Heavy Industries
sections.summary: Coke 136,800 tons, postwar-peak pig iron and steel at 60 percent of minimum need, aluminum 1,869 tons, plus copper, rubber, cement, fertilizer, chemicals and machinery.

sections.title: Section 4. Manufacturing
sections.summary: Food-processing shortages, pulp up 36 percent, paper 34,168 short tons, plus glass, medical supplies, electrical goods, truck chassis, leather, handicrafts and sewing machines.

sections.title: Section 5. Textile Industries
sections.summary: Raw silk reached a postwar peak; cotton, rayon, wool and knit-goods output rose on eased power limits and better coal and raw-material deliveries.

sections.title: Section 6. Transportation and Public Utilities
sections.summary: Government railways carried 270,899,116 passengers and 9,433,500 tons of freight in March; electric power generated 2,432,541,000 kWh, up 21 percent; gas industry data.

sections.title: Section 7. Communications
sections.summary: New Labor Bureau at the Communications Ministry, 44 radio stations licensed, radiotelegraph to the United States opened 18 April, and 5,700,000 licensed receivers.

sections.title: Section 8. Labor
sections.summary: Employment exchanges reorganized 8 April; 19,983 unions with 5,326,969 members; coal miners' agreement of 12 April; Central Labor Relations Committee elections; employment programs.

sections.title: Section 9. Imports and Exports
sections.summary: Little change in March trade; sample shipments included 40 cases of crabmeat to the United States and textile, machinery, chemical and wood products to Europe and Asia.

sections.title: Section 10. Rationing and Price Control
sections.summary: Government food stocks of 38 days, 4,153,369 tons of rice collected, 112,026 tons of imports released, electric rates up 300 percent, and new salt, lime, coke and petroleum prices.

sections.title: Section 11. Finance
sections.summary: Bank of Japan notes at 122.4 billion yen; licenses to Times Publishing, Northwest and Pan American; income-tax estimate raised to 16 billion yen; April borrowing of 12,910,624,720 yen.

sections.title: Section 12. Property Control
sections.summary: Allied and looted property tallies, dissolved organizations' accounts, the 31 March antitrust act with a Fair Trade Commission, and 65 holding companies' shares worth 5.15 billion yen.

sections.title: Antitrust and Cartels
sections.summary: 26 restricted concerns allowed 82,675,838 yen for rehabilitation; the new antitrust act's prohibitions and seven-member Fair Trade Commission; zaibatsu family designations.

sections.title: Part IV: Social
sections.summary: Health, nutrition and repatriation figures (62,327 repatriated, 35 typhus cases in Tokyo), then education, religion, information programs and press comment for April 1947.

sections.title: Section 1. Public Health and Welfare
sections.summary: February nutrition surveys showed improvement; 35 typhus cases in Tokyo; 3,172 hospitals; patent medicine output of 117,497,793 yen; 62,327 Japanese repatriated.

sections.title: Section 2. Education, Religion and Media of Expression
sections.summary: Teacher-training conferences, shrine and temple land notification of 2 April, election broadcasting, 18,000,000 Constitution pamphlets, press comment and 17,142 visitors to the SCAP library.
